title: Why convictions for animal cruelty remain so rare
p1:
Many people assume that harming an animal automatically leads to serious punishment.

But the reality is very different. Thousands of cruelty cases are reported, yet convictions often remain uncommon.
p2:
The surprising reason is not always the absence of laws. The bigger challenge is proving the case.

Animal cruelty cases often depend on evidence: medical reports, witnesses, documentation, and proof of intent. Without strong evidence, even a disturbing incident can become difficult to prosecute.
p3:
Another overlooked issue is that many laws were created decades ago and may not reflect how society views animal welfare today. Awareness, timely reporting, and better investigation methods can make a major difference.

A complaint is only the first step. Turning concern into accountability requires evidence, enforcement, and public pressure.
conclusion: Do you think stricter laws alone can reduce animal cruelty, or is better enforcement the bigger solution?
